conditions.description: Selected work is technically stopped in the observed local persistent stock workflows. Cleanup holds maintenance and complete root and actual spawn-descendant writer ownership through fresh validation. Independent work may continue.

Related selected-thread metadata updates and dependency-reference publication, including a new fork history reference, must finish before cleanup. Acquiring a writer guard does not independently certify their completion.
The selected rollout locations and every affected database and log location use the qualified local filesystem and cooperative writer and SQLite locks.
No NFS or cross-host filesystem behavior is covered, and no offline database cutover or arbitrary operator replacement may run concurrently.
A catalogue activity label, age or a writer-lock observation alone does not certify quiescence; exact native ownership and fresh execution checks remain required.
This scoped assessment does not certify historical-body integrity, a complete Core lifecycle, generic Rust equivalence or the source and signature of an observed producer binary.
Only qualified owner, provider, attachment and Guardian representations are covered; unsupported Internal Guardian selections remain protected or refused.
This record does not establish producer binary identity, verify its own origin, prove current quiescence or authorize a cleanup operation.

The actual producer and helper use matching qualified roots for the state database, companion databases, logs and selected rollout locations. Neither this record nor the helper request independently observes that the producer uses those locations.
Ordinary cache, plugin, process and output paths do not alias selected storage locations.

Stock tests used a local scripted model provider and the observed 0.172.0 producer. Additional Guardian and attachment representations have disposable storage-fixture coverage. All clients deleting from a home must use the Keep-capable helper to enforce Keep marks.
The observed producer executable digest identifies the executable exercised. It does not attest the build provenance of a caller-provided producer.

The released profile covers the ordinary on-disk agent board. A home using the separate Guardian V3 board message_board_guardian_1.sqlite is outside this cleanup assessment. Check the effective producer SQLite directory and its configuration separately from doctor.
Realtime storage checks cover seeded canonical rows and retained stock reads. Live voice transport and the full checkpoint rollback and realtime recovery lifecycle were not qualified.

review.scope: Selected technically stopped persistent local work produced by stock Codex CLI 0.172.0 on the qualified Ubuntu 26.04 LTS x86_64 host. witnesses.scope: Matched wire-7 helper and Keep. Disposable native storage fixtures cover qualified representation, ownership, writer and exact-effect checks.
V1 legacy on stock 0.172.0 refused a live writer, removed only the stopped child, and let an unrelated turn complete. A retained parent resumed.
V2 legacy on stock 0.172.0 refused a live writer, removed only the stopped child, and let an unrelated turn complete. A retained parent resumed.
V2 paginated on stock 0.172.0 refused a live writer, removed only the stopped child, and let an unrelated turn complete. A retained parent resumed.
The installed CLI enforced Keep and removed one selected child after the mark was cleared. The installed MCP removed one child and returned the original outcome after restart without re-dispatch.

Stock Codex projected explicit canonical realtime seed records from the parent and child. The installed GC removed only the selected child’s rows and rollout. The retained parent returned the same realtime page from a fresh producer.

A stock V2 parent accepted a test child reply before interruption. The helper refused the live work, then removed the selected child after shutdown. The next turn in the retained parent observed the reply exactly once.
The preview protected the provider required by a paginated fork. After exact removal of a sibling child, both retained rollouts kept their bytes and a fresh stock process read and resumed them.
A stock revert wrote a different physical rollout ID. The installed plan identified both the original and current rollout as one logical thread’s history.
The published helper preserved an unrelated root, bounded ordinary board cleanup, rejected the old schema and extra trigger, and prevented late root writes in native storage fixtures.
A fresh app-server discovered the server, called the installed compatibility tool in its first test thread, and called it again from a second thread in the same process.
